Subject: Planning renewal: multi-year + co-term across teams

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re starting to formalize NexaHealth’s renewal and expansion asks for a Jan 1, 2027 start. A few constraints on our side:
- We want co-terming across the product suite (hosted API for burst capacity + dedicated pools for production inference).
- Expected token consumption profile: ~3x growth year-over-year, but ramp will be front-loaded (first 6 months 60% growth, then flatten).
- We need a clear opt-out option on auto-renew (procurement requires an explicit review window).

Could you share 1) a co-term proposal that covers multi-year pricing and staged ramp schedules, 2) any onboarding credits or short-term consumption credits you can apply for a fast ramp, and 3) what the SLO / credit language looks like if we move to Dedicated?

I’ve attached a high-level forecast for Q1–Q4 2027. Happy to hop on a call Thursday if that helps.

Thanks,
Emma Liu
Director, Platform Integrations
NexaHealth

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Planning renewal: multi-year + co-term across teams

Hi Emma — great to get the forecast, and appreciate the timing. High level, we can support the scenarios you described. I sketched three options below so procurement and finance have something tangible to react to: 

Option A — 2yr co-term (recommended for predictability)
- Co-term both Hosted API and Dedicated capacity under a single contract with a shared renewal date (Jan 1, 2029).
- Staged ramp schedule baked into the SKU: months 1–3 = baseline + 40% burst, months 4–6 = baseline + 100% (apply onboarding credits to months 1–3), months 7–12 = baseline + target growth to meet the 3x FY expectation.
- Pricing: blended per-token floor with annual true-up; 8–12% discount on hosted unit rate compared to standard list when committed for 2 years.
- Auto-renew: contract can include a 60-day renewal review window (opt-out allowed with written notice) to satisfy procurement.

Option B — 1yr with auto-renew opt-out (lower commitment flexibility)
- Higher per-token rate, but no long-term co-terming requirement. Good if procurement insists on annual renewals.

Option C — Dedicated-first with overflow to Hosted (throughput guarantee + overflow surcharge)
- Dedicated pool with guaranteed throughput and an overflow band to Hosted at a known surcharge. Best for latency-sensitive workloads.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal pricing worksheet (attached) — outlines the blended rates and a simple ramp P&L.
2) Draft SOW and renewal exhibit to capture ramp milestones and acceptance gates (attached).
3) Short call: I’m available Thu 10/22 at 10:00am PT or Fri 10/23 at 9:00am PT to walk through options and agree on a preferred path.

I’ve attached: NexaHealth_Renewal_Draft_20261020.pdf, pricing_worksheet_nexai.xlsx, and a draft SOW. Let me know which time works.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Agreed tentative path (subject to final SOW/DocuSign):
- Term: 2 years co-term starting Jan 1, 2027 (renewal date Jan 1, 2029).
- Ramp: apply onboarding credit for months 1–3; target staged ramp with checkpoints at month 3 and month 6 tied to usage true-ups.
- Pricing: 10% committed discount on hosted units with a 5% onboarding credit applied to Q1 spend; Dedicated pools priced with an SLA credit clause (P99 credit = 10% of monthly committed spend for qualifying breaches).
- Auto-renew: include a 60-day review/opt-out window to satisfy procurement.
